question: Illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing in the Mediterranean Sea represents a major threat to marine ecosystems. Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/21961 and Implementing Regulation (EC) No 1224/20092, as amended by Council Regulation (EU) 2023/28423, govern access to waters and resources, fisheries control and surveillance, inspections, and enforcement of the common fisheries policy.

In Italy, over 50 % of fishery product landings are estimated to originate from illegal activities. According to data from the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, 58 % of monitored fish stocks in the Mediterranean are overexploited. Despite improvements since 2012, overfishing, IUU fishing and accidental catches continue to exert significant pressure on ecosystems and coastal communities.

Controls along the Tyrrhenian coast of Italy have also revealed cases of poaching involving unauthorised nets and traps. Without more sustainable fisheries, some stocks risk collapse, with serious environmental and economic consequences. Given the above: What is the current state of the implementation and enforcement of the regulations referred to above?
